ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, $\odot O$ is the circumcircle of the right-angled triangle $ABC$, with the diameter $AC=4$. A tangent line is drawn through point $C$ to $\odot O$, intersecting the extended line of $AB$ at point $D$. $M$ is the midpoint of $CD$, and lines $BM$ and $OM$ are drawn, with $BC$ and $OM$ intersecting at point $N$. $BM$ is tangent to $\odot O$; when $\angle BAC=60^\circ$, what is the area of the shape enclosed by chord $AB$ and arc $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle BAC=60^\circ$ and $OA=OB$, \\
it follows that $\triangle ABO$ is an equilateral triangle, \\
which implies that $\angle AOB=60^\circ$.\\
Given that $AC=4$, it follows that $OA=2$,\\
therefore, the area of the region bounded by chord $AB$ and arc $AB$ $=S_{\text{sector}}AOB-S_{\triangle}AOB$\\
$=\frac{60^\circ\pi \times 2^2}{360^\circ}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\times 2^2=\boxed{\frac{2\pi}{3}-\sqrt{3}}$
